headline: Nvidia's Huang reinstated; vCenter zero-day and Azure secrets leak drive patch urgency
overview: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO after White House input cleared him of national security concerns, drawing sharp political scrutiny. On the security side, a VMware vCenter flaw exploited since September and an Azure API Management secrets leak dominated, alongside a run of breaches and AI-accelerated attacks.

topStories.title: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO amid unresolved investigation
topStories.summary: Nvidia's board reinstated Huang after senior US officials said his return posed no national security risk, and the White House backed the decision. An independent investigation remains open, and critics in Congress are pressing for answers on export controls.

topStories.title: VMware vCenter zero-day exploited since September
topStories.summary: A critical vCenter authentication bypass was used by a suspected China-linked group months before public disclosure, with a custom tool able to extract directory data, forge SAML tokens and create admin accounts. CISA added it to its exploited list with a same-day federal deadline.

topStories.title: Azure API Management classic tier leaks secrets used against Norwegian energy firms
topStories.summary: Norwegian authorities reported attacks on energy companies exploiting a flaw in Azure API Management that could expose stored secrets and keys. Microsoft deployed a mitigation, but customers should confirm they run the patched version.

topStories.title: AI agents accelerate attacks and push defenders to tighten controls
topStories.summary: Amazon reported AI agents used by attackers found and exploited a zero-day in a medical imaging server in about eleven minutes. Several US banks responded by restricting AI agent access, adding monitoring and kill switches, and treating agents like staff.

topStories.title: Major data breaches across healthcare, retail, utilities and telecoms
topStories.summary: PRISM Medical reported exposure of data on 1.3 million people, Korean utility Kepco lost records on over 1.5 million customers, and Bell and the European Commission disclosed data theft. Next confirmed a third-party supplier breach.

topStories.title: Nginx, SonicWall and Entra flaws demand immediate action
topStories.summary: Public exploit code appeared for several Nginx flaws affecting Veeam and Cisco products. SonicWall is retiring Gen 6 firewalls, and Microsoft disclosed a Entra Connect Health flaw exposing admin emails and tenant metadata, which may lead to phishing.

episodes.title: A perfect storm of imperfect systems.
episodes.summary: Covers a run of tech outages, banks restricting AI agents, a European Commission data leak, Next's supplier breach, the PRISM Medical breach and the Azure flaw hitting Norwegian energy firms. Also covers funding and M&A and follow-ups on USDA, FBI and NSA incidents, plus an interview on US cyber leadership changes.

episodes.title: Jensen returns under scrutiny, CrowdStrike's $44B Zscaler deal, KEPCO breach hits 1.5M
episodes.summary: Covers Huang's return at Nvidia, CrowdStrike's proposed $43.9 billion Zscaler deal, the Kepco breach affecting 1.5 million people, cyber leadership nominations, AI-speed attacks, La Liga and Bell data incidents, and a Bulgarian government intrusion.

episodes.title: Azure API Management Classic Secrets Leak; iTerm2 Kitty Protocol RCE; binary-parser Code Injection (CVE-2026-134814) (Nov 24th 2026)
episodes.summary: Covers the Azure API Management secrets exposure, a terminal escape issue in iTerm2 that can lead to code execution when viewing files, and a binary-parser flaw that was not fully fixed earlier this year.

episodes.title: Too Big to Fire: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO
episodes.summary: Traces the sequence of events leading to Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia, the White House role, market reaction and political debate over state versus private power in AI.

episodes.title: Bitcoin came for Kentucky’s coal country. Now AI wants in.
episodes.summary: Sponsored-free feature on how Bitcoin mining and now AI data centres have affected eastern Kentucky's economy. The notes give no detail beyond this and do not cover cyber security directly.

episodes.title: Episode 21: Cyber Threats in Aisle 404
episodes.summary: Covers a VMware vCenter flaw exploited as a zero-day by a suspected China-linked group, along with an ASP.NET security library exposing remote code execution and a supermarket breach in Australia. The transcript is cut off before the later stories.

episodes.title: The No Good, Very Bad Week for Infrastructure - The 443 Podcast - Episode 397
episodes.summary: Looks back at a chaotic stretch of outages, including a Microsoft outage, US flight disruptions and problems at banks and intelligence networks, and briefly discusses the Nginx flaw.

episodes.title: FBI Crime Database Hacked
episodes.summary: Covers a hack of an FBI crime database, with limited confirmed information so far and speculation about who was responsible.

episodes.title: Entra Connect Health breach, AI agents find a zero-day, SAP exploited | Cyber Security News Nov 23
episodes.summary: Covers the Entra Connect Health breach, SAP NetWeaver exploitation, public Nginx exploit code affecting Veeam and Cisco, GL.iNet malware, SonicWall Gen 6 retirement, OpenRouter leaking prompts, and AI agents exploiting a MONAI Label zero-day.

episodes.title: vCenter Zero-Day Exploited, Entra Metadata Leak, New Cyber Director
episodes.summary: Covers the vCenter zero-day now on CISA's exploited list, the Entra Connect Health flaw, the new acting National Cyber Director, and the Amazon AI-agent zero-day finding, with some additional third-party confirmations.
